source_text:
Τοιαῦτα τὰ κατὰ τὸν μακάριον Πολύκαρπον, ὃς σὺν τοῖς ἀπὸ Φιλαδελφίας δωδέκατος ἐν Σμύρνῃ μαρτυρήσας, μόνος ὑπὸ πάντων μᾶλλον μνημονεύεται, ὥστε καὶ ὑπὸ τῶν ἐθνῶν ἐν παντὶ τόπῳ λαλεῖσθαι: οὐ μόνον διδάσκαλος γενόμενος ἐπίσημος, ἀλλὰ καὶ μάρτυς ἔξοχος, οὗ τὸ μαρτύριον πάντες ἐπιθυμοῦσιν μιμεῖσθαι κατὰ τὸ εὐαγγέλιον Χριστοῦ γενόμενον.
διὰ τῆς ὑπομονῆς καταγωνισάμενος τὸν ἄδικον ἄρχοντα καὶ οὕτως τὸν τῆς ἀφθαρσίας στέφανον ἀπολαβών, σὺν τοῖς ἀποστόλοις καὶ πᾶσιν δικαίοις ἀγαλλιώμενος δοξάζει τὸν θεὸν καὶ πατέρα παντοκράτορα καὶ εὐλογεῖ τὸν κύριον ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦν Χριστόν, τὸν σωτῆρα τῶν ψυχῶν ἡμῶν καὶ κυβερνήτην τῶν σωμάτων ἡμῶν καὶ ποιμένα τῆς κατὰ τὴν οἰκουμένην καθολικῆς ἐκκλησίας.
thought_title: Polycarp's unique renown and heavenly reward
orientation: The church of Smyrna closes its account of Polycarp's martyrdom by praising his singular fame and his present glory with God.
pass_a_gloss: Such [are] the things concerning the blessed Polycarp, who with the [ones] from Philadelphia [as] twelfth in Smyrna having borne witness, alone by all more is remembered, so that also by the nations in every place [he] is spoken of: not only [a] teacher having become distinguished, but also [a] martyr outstanding, whose martyrdom all desire to imitate according to the gospel of Christ having happened. Through endurance having overcome the unjust ruler and thus the crown of immortality having received, with the apostles and all [the] righteous rejoicing [he] glorifies God and Father almighty and blesses our Lord Jesus Christ, the savior of our souls and pilot of our bodies and shepherd of the catholic church throughout the inhabited world.

choices.why: The glossary reserves 'martyr' for μάρτυς and 'martyrdom' for μαρτύριον; the participle here is the verb form, so a verbal rendering keeps the distinction clear.
Fixed glossary rendering for στέφανος τῆς ἀφθαρσίας.
Fixed glossary rendering for καθολικὴ ἐκκλησία.
The metaphor is nautical (steersman of a ship); 'pilot' preserves the image better than a general term.
ἄρχων here refers to the proconsul who condemned Polycarp; 'ruler' keeps the general term while 'unjust' preserves the moral judgment.

pass_b_english: Such is the story of the blessed Polycarp. He was the twelfth person to be martyred in Smyrna, together with those from Philadelphia in Asia, yet he alone is remembered more than all the rest. Even the pagans speak of him in every place. He was not only a distinguished teacher but also an outstanding martyr, and everyone desires to imitate his martyrdom because it followed the gospel of Christ.

By his endurance Polycarp overcame the unjust ruler, and in this way he received the crown of immortality. Now he rejoices with the apostles and all the righteous. He glorifies God the Father Almighty and blesses our Lord Jesus Christ, the Savior of our souls, the helmsman of our bodies, and the shepherd of the catholic church throughout the world.

last_rejected.why: Glossary requires 'provincial official' for Ἀσιάρχης but this is κυβερνήτης, not in glossary; however 'pilot' is archaic for 'governor/steersman'. No glossary violation.
last_rejected.ruling: κυβερνήτης means 'pilot/steersman'; 'pilot' is standard, not archaic. No glossary issue.

last_rejected.quote: the shepherd of the catholic church throughout the world
last_rejected.source_quote: ποιμένα τῆς κατὰ τὴν οἰκουμένην καθολικῆς ἐκκλησίας
last_rejected.why: Missing 'God and' before 'Father Almighty'; source has θεὸν καὶ πατέρα παντοκράτορα.
last_rejected.ruling: Source θεὸν καὶ πατέρα παντοκράτορα is rendered 'God the Father Almighty' earlier in the sentence; not omitted.

polish.changed: Clarified that Polycarp is the subject of the final sentence, split long clauses into natural modern sentences, and made the flow easier to follow aloud without altering any claims.
Clarified that Philadelphia is in Asia, kept all claims and titles intact, and smoothed sentence flow for public reading.

notes.why: Philadelphia is not explained; reader may confuse it with the American city.
notes.fix: Note this is Philadelphia in Asia Minor (modern Alaşehir, Turkey).

problems.why: “Pilot” is an odd metaphor for Christ’s role; likely meant “guardian” or “shepherd.”
problems.fix: Change to “the guardian of our bodies” or “the shepherd of our bodies.”

problems.why: 'Pilot' for Christ is unusual; Greek 'κυβερνήτης' = helmsman, governor.

fixed: Changed 'pilot' to 'helmsman' to reflect the Greek 'κυβερνήτης' more clearly; both reported problems concern the same phrase.
